model.description:
Toolkit is a set of everyday design utilities in one plugin. Open it, pick a tool, get the job done.


TOOLS INCLUDED


PixelPort - Lossless Import

Bring big images and PDFs into Figma at full resolution. Figma downscales anything over 4096px on its longest edge a 2560x9529 screenshot becomes 1100x4096 and loses most of its detail. PixelPort auto-tiles the image into slices under the limit and reassembles them, so every pixel is preserved. Import PNG, JPG, WEBP, GIF and PDF; multi-file; PDFs page by page at your DPI.


Font Swapper - Find, review & replace fonts

Scan a frame, page, or the whole file to see every font in use, where and how much. Replace a whole family (styles mapped automatically) or a single style, with a live preview. Catches fonts inside mixed-font layers, flags missing fonts, and locates usage across pages. Never silently substitutes a weight.


Color Swap - Find & replace colors

Scan for every solid color in use, then swap it for another color, a Figma variable, or a paint style. Locate where a color is used, spot near-duplicates and raw-vs-tokenized colors, and clean up your palette. Undoable.


Iconry - Browse & import icons

Browse the open-source icon set and import icons as reusable component sets, auto-sorted by category on a tidy library page. Restyle by size and color, bind to a variable, and drag icons straight onto your canvas.


PRIVACY

PixelPort, Font Swapper and Color Swap process everything locally on your device. Iconry fetches icon SVGs from the public jsDelivr CDN so you can browse and import them; no design data is ever sent anywhere.

model.description:
Release notes


v1.2 — a much bigger toolkit

• Type on a Path — click a path and type. Four effects, align-to-path, curve spacing, flip. Syncs as live, editable Figma text.

• Pathfinder — all eight boolean operations.

• Per-object appearance — each shape keeps its own fill, stroke and weight, so recolouring one no longer recolours everything.

• Rotation — drag just outside a corner of the selection, or rotate and flip numerically.

• Ruler guides — drag them off the rulers, Alt-drag to duplicate.

• Smart guides that align to other geometry, plus grid and guide toggles.

• Join two end points with Cmd/Ctrl+J, or merge them into one point with Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+Shift+J.

• Contextual bar for anchor actions: convert, mirror handles, add/remove, join.

• Paste SVG or path data onto the canvas, or drop an SVG file on it.

• Import several selected Figma vectors at once.

• Resizable plugin window, remembered between sessions.

• Redo (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z), D for default paint, Shift+X to swap fill and stroke, [ and ] for stroke weight.


BetterPath brings Illustrator's path tools into Figma.


Figma's API can't replace the native canvas tools, so BetterPath gives you a proper drawing surface inside the plugin — built on Paper.js, which models paths the way Illustrator does — then rebuilds what you drew as native Figma vectors you can keep editing with Figma's own pen.


TOOLS


Select (V) — Move, scale from the bounding box, or rotate by dragging just outside a corner. Alt-drag duplicates, Alt-resize scales from the centre, Shift constrains. Double-click a shape to edit its points.


Pen (P) — Click for a corner, drag for a smooth point. Alt breaks the handle pair, Shift constrains to 45°. Click a segment to add an anchor, an anchor to remove one, a loose end to resume drawing, the first anchor to close.


Curvature (C) — Drop points and the curve is solved to pass through all of them. Double-click a point to toggle corner and smooth.


Width (W) — Drag on a path to thicken or thin it at that point. Figma has no variable stroke, so the profile is expanded into a filled outline on sync.


Type (T) — Click a path and type. Rainbow, Skew, Stair Step and Gravity effects, align to baseline/ascender/descender/centre, and spacing that tightens on curves. Drag the bracket to slide the run, or across the path to flip it.


Direct (A) — Marquee individual anchors, drag any one to move the group, or drag a segment to reshape it. A contextual bar appears with Convert, Handles, Add/Remove anchors and Join.


PATHFINDER


Unite, Minus Front, Intersect, Exclude, Divide, Trim, Crop and Minus Back.


SYMMETRY


Mirror on one or both axes, radial and grid repeats, previewed live. Drag the axis where you want it, type exact coordinates, snap it to the grid, then lock it so it stays put while you draw.


PRECISION


Configurable grid, ruler guides you drag off the rulers (Alt-drag to duplicate one), smart guides that align to other geometry, and snapping to the grid, anchors, path edges and the symmetry axis. Non-destructive Simplify. Rotate and flip numerically. 60 steps of undo and redo.


EVERY OBJECT IS SEPARATE


Each shape keeps its own fill, stroke and weight. Select one and change it without touching the rest; with nothing selected, your choices become the defaults for the next thing you draw.


MOVING WORK IN AND OUT


Select vectors in Figma and import them for editing, paste SVG or path data straight onto the canvas, or drop an SVG file on it. Sync writes back a real VectorNetwork you can keep editing with Figma's pen, or imports via SVG if you prefer — replacing the node you selected or placing a new one. Path type syncs as live Figma text, one node per character, still editable with its real font.


Resize the plugin window from the corner grip; the size is remembered.


GOOD TO KNOW


• Variable width exports as a filled outline, not a stroke — that's the only way Figma can represent it.

• Symmetry copies are transforms of the source, so they stay one object until you sync.

• Illustrator's 3D Ribbon type effect isn't included: it needs a per-character shear that a Figma text node can't express.

• The outline offset doesn't fully resolve self-intersections on very tight curves at very heavy widths.


Made by MarkDo — markdo27.github.io

model.description:
Icon Library Toolkit gets your icons from Figma to developers without the back-and-forth.


Pick some layers, a page or the whole file, and press Scan. The plugin finds your icons, shows each one at a readable size, and flags common problems such as text inside an icon, shadows, default layer names or duplicate names. When you’re ready, choose the formats you need and download one ZIP with a short guide for developers inside.


Your file is never changed during a scan. A few optional features can edit it, such as turning a loose frame into a component. They stay off until you enable Labs, always show a preview first, and apply as a single undo step.


Features

--------------------------------------------------------------

For designers

Scan what you choose. The current selection, a page or the whole file.

See icons clearly. Large previews with S / M / L sizes, a grid view, and a hover preview showing how an icon looks at 16, 24 and 32 px on light, dark or checker backgrounds.

Know what’s wrong. An Issues tab lists problems with a short “How to fix” note. Select the affected layer in Figma with one click.

Stay in control. Include or leave out icons before exporting, and rename an icon for the export without touching Figma.

Find hidden problems. It flags icons with the same drawing, mismatched layer names that break colour overrides, and layers left out of the scan.

Fix some problems for you (Labs, optional). Replace a detached icon with an instance, or turn a frame into a component. You see before and after previews, and one undo reverts the batch.

For design system managers

Library health at a glance. A status line and an Issues tab that shows what needs attention before a release.

Consistent naming and structure. Names are turned into clean, predictable ones. You choose how duplicates are handled: stop the export, add a category, or add a number.

Categories from your file. Icons are grouped using your layer names, sections, frames or pages.

Changes since last time. Compare with your last export (kept on your computer, saved in the file, or read from your repository). See what is new, renamed or redrawn, with a suggested version number and a changelog.

Renames don’t break apps. An icon is tracked by its component, so a renamed icon keeps working under its old name for a while.

Intentional duplicates. Mark two names for one drawing as intentional, and the export stores the artwork once.

Share settings. Export your settings as a file, or publish them in the Figma file so everyone exports the same way.

Choose how colours and strokes behave. Tie colours to your Figma variables or design tokens, and set stroke weight to stay constant, scale, or follow a size table.


For developers

Formats.

SVG files and an SVG sprite

A searchable preview page

Angular (17.1+ and 14+) and React components

A framework-free Web Component

Optional CSS mask classes and Code Connect templates

Themeable by CSS. Change colour, size and stroke width with CSS variables. Icons can have several colours.

Built for real apps. Import only the icons you use. Icons used by name load in small chunks by category. Angular also has a sprite option. All names are typed.

Machine-readable. icons.json lists every icon, and the ZIP includes a README and a guide for AI assistants.

Dev Mode. Select an icon to copy code for Angular, React, HTML or Web Component. An inspect panel lists the icons in a selection and downloads a ZIP of just those.

Send straight to your project (Labs, optional). A small helper running on your computer can write the files into a project folder and commit them with git.
